newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest air cargo delays now seen up to 3-4 days.
newsitem.headline: Budapest air cargo delays now seen up to 3-4 days.

text.p: New regulations at Budapest's Ferihegy Airport are now seen causing delays of three to four days in customs clearing imported cargo, and problems could last another two weeks, airlines and freight forwarders said on Wednesday.
When the rules took effect on Monday, airlines said they had hoped the complications would lead to only one-day delays in clearance.
"It should take about two weeks for customs authorities to resume normal operations," one airline official said.
"The problem is that shippers pay a premium to deliver goods by air because their goods are special or urgent, so the main advantage of air transport is undermined by these delays," he added.
The delays stem from the new regulations, which require customs authorities to record more detail about incoming cargo before clearing the goods for release.
The airport receives an average of 300 cargo shipments a day, and the goods are usually cleared within 24 hours, freight forwarders at the airport said.
But the new regulations have slowed the daily clearance to roughly 60 shipments, resulting in delays of three or four days in the release of most goods.
Officials from the airport authority LRI were unavailable for comment.
